chapter: Pianists, the district and Stormy Weather
title: Simon Trajan, Saeed and Joe Robichaud's father
summary: After a tape pause: the Trajan brothers, Joe Robichaud and playing with his father's big band.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Did you run out of tape, Conor?
Yeah. And what I still have, I want to say for Simon. Yeah, sure.
Simon, is his name Simon Trajan? Yeah.
I don't know him too. You ever see him?

Yeah. He used to come and play, and I used to go down this name, Simon. He's a wino too. No, I played with him already. He'd been right around the corner yet some way. Simon Trajan. And he got another brother. He played his piano. What's your good? Good piano. Real good. I know Saeed.
Saeed, he's a drummer.
Yeah.
I was talking to Saeed. It was what, it was Sam? Wasn't it Sam? I can't remember all the brothers. Neither me.
But I remember, I remember one of the brothers. He died. He died. A lot of those guys died. He used to play around. He used to play at the Preservation. He died too. I used to play with his daddy.
What's his name?
What did he play?
Piano.
He was a good piano player.
Joe Robichaud. Joe Robichaud.
And he had a left-hand violin player.
And you used to play with his dad?
He used to play with his dad. We played at the Lundish Young Russell on, what you call it, straight? You know what I love? Iberville. Iberville and Dorfey. Between Bourbon and Rock.
Yeah.
It's right on the corner, right?
Well, it may have been then, but the one I know is.
The one I know, that, I played there with him. He said, that man behind us.
Did he have a band or just two people? He hired me to play.

He had a big band. He had a big band. Yeah, a big band. He introduced me as a banjo player off the coast of California. And then I played at the Crescent and the Tulane Table. That was Joe Robichaud's dad. Just large, been a long time. Pico was the one that told us about him. He wanted a banjo player. He had a banjo player. He could hire me, and he hired me. Four men in a row of shoes.
